paragraphs: Open-world semi-supervised learning involves recognizing familiar categories while also discovering unfamiliar ones in unlabeled data. The labeled examples describe only the known categories, so the central question is how that partial knowledge can help organize a broader collection. This paper develops a graph-based mathematical framework for studying that question.

The framework connects clustering to graph factorization and supports an algorithm called Spectral Open-world Representation Learning, or SORL. The authors show that minimizing their training loss is equivalent to a spectral decomposition of the graph. This connects the representations learned by the algorithm to a mathematical operation whose clustering behavior can be analyzed.

Using that equivalence, the authors derive an error bound covering both known and novel classes and investigate when labeled data helps. Their benchmark experiments show that SORL can match or outperform several strong comparison methods. The contribution therefore combines a practical learning method with theoretical tools for understanding its behavior, including the circumstances in which existing labels benefit discovery.
neurips-2023-a-graph-theoretic-framework.tldr: A graph-based framework connects open-world learning to spectral decomposition, yielding clustering guarantees and a competitive practical algorithm.

paragraphs: This paper studies recovering two hidden matrices from their noisy product when their rank grows in proportion to their dimensions. In this regime, the hidden structure becomes larger as the matrices grow. The authors investigate how accurately the factors can be reconstructed and what estimators might reach the statistical limits of the problem.

Their Bayesian analysis assumes that one factor is symmetric, that both factors and the additive noise have rotationally invariant prior distributions, and that those priors are known. Under these assumptions, they derive analytical formulas for rotation-invariant estimators. The derivation combines random matrix theory, spherical integrals, and the replica method from statistical mechanics.

The authors conjecture that these estimators minimize average mean-square error in the large-dimension limit. Numerical comparisons with oracle estimators support that conjecture; the oracles use ground-truth information and are optimal by definition. The distinction matters: the paper supplies estimator formulas and numerical evidence of optimality, while the broader optimality statement remains a conjecture within the stated Bayesian setting.
neurips-2023-bayesian-extensive-rank-mat.tldr: The paper derives Bayesian matrix-factor estimators under rotationally invariant priors and provides numerical support for their conjectured large-dimension optimality.

paragraphs: Understanding a 3D point cloud requires relating many points while preserving the geometry of nearby surfaces. Global transformer attention becomes impractical for clouds containing more than 100,000 points, and even local cubic or spherical windows can require many pairwise comparisons. Standard linear projections for attention also do not explicitly model local 3D structure.

ConDaFormer changes the shape of the attention calculation by splitting a cubic window into three perpendicular two-dimensional planes. This reduces the number of points involved while covering a similar spatial range. The design can extend attention farther without increasing computational complexity, although the split leaves out some contextual relationships.

To address that loss, the authors add depth-wise convolutions before and after attention. These local structure enhancements also capture geometric information that ordinary attention projections overlook. Together, the components aim to combine broader contextual relationships with nearby geometric detail. Experiments across several point-cloud understanding benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the design, supporting this combination of reduced attention cost and explicit local structure.
neurips-2023-condaformer-disassembled-tr.tldr: ConDaFormer reduces 3D attention costs with perpendicular planar windows and adds local convolutions to capture geometry and recover context.

paragraphs: Bayesian inverse problems seek a distribution of possible unknowns consistent with observed data. This paper considers linear inverse problems where those unknowns are functions in an infinite-dimensional space. Existing diffusion approaches in this setting mainly learn unconditional scores, and their posterior sampling procedures can require many costly evaluations of the forward operator.

The authors propose an amortized conditional diffusion method that learns to support posterior sampling directly. Their central theoretical result establishes that a conditional denoising estimator used successfully in finite dimensions can also apply in infinite dimensions. This provides a mathematical foundation for bringing that estimation approach into function-space inference.

The extension requires care because the conditional score typically becomes unbounded near small diffusion times, unlike the unconditional score. Addressing this behavior is a substantial part of the analysis. Stylized and large-scale numerical examples validate the proposed approach and demonstrate discretization-invariant Bayesian inference. The contribution connects practical conditional sampling with an analysis that explicitly handles the difficulties introduced by infinite-dimensional unknowns.
neurips-2023-conditional-score-based-dif.tldr: The paper establishes a conditional diffusion approach to infinite-dimensional Bayesian linear inverse problems, including theory for conditional score estimation.

paragraphs: Many datasets describe events unfolding in continuous time, with multiple dependent pieces of information inside each event. Medical records are one example. Applying generative pretrained transformers to these sequences requires tools for preparing the data, representing internal event structure, and evaluating how useful the resulting models are for later tasks.

Event Stream GPT provides an open-source library covering that workflow. Users specify a minimal configuration to construct flexible datasets at foundation-model scale. A modeling interface compatible with Hugging Face supports transformers for this type of data, incorporates causal dependencies within events, and enables autoregressive generation of event sequences.

The library also standardizes evaluation on user-defined fine-tuning tasks, including assessments with few examples or no task-specific examples. These are evaluation capabilities, rather than a claim that every model will perform well in those settings. The contribution is infrastructure that makes continuous-time event modeling easier to construct and assess, addressing a tooling gap that has hindered the use of foundation models beyond language.
neurips-2023-event-stream-gpt-a-data-pre.tldr: Event Stream GPT provides data preparation, transformer modeling, and standardized evaluation tools for continuous-time sequences of internally dependent events.

paragraphs: Distribution shift can change both how frequently examples occur and which examples are possible at all. The latter concerns distribution support. Ordinary importance weighting handles matching supports or a training support that covers the test support, but it can fail when test examples occupy regions absent from training.

Generalized importance weighting addresses this by dividing the test support into regions inside and outside the training support. It decomposes expected risk into a weighted classification term for the shared region and a standard classification term for the outside region. The authors establish risk consistency through this decomposition, and the formulation reduces to ordinary importance weighting when training support covers testing.

The implementation uses a one-class support vector machine to split validation data. An existing importance-weighting algorithm handles the inside portion using training and validation examples, while the outside portion contributes its own classification term. Experiments report improvements over importance-weighting methods when test support extends beyond training support or overlaps only partially, supporting the framework across the four support relationships considered.
neurips-2023-generalizing-importance-wei.tldr: Generalized importance weighting separates shared and unseen support regions to address distribution shifts that ordinary importance weighting cannot fully cover.

paragraphs: Sequential recommenders use a person's interaction history to suggest the next item. Many train by distinguishing a positive item from sampled negative items. This paper argues that noisy or easily rejected negatives can weaken the preference signal, and proposes instead to generate an idealized item representing what the user might want.

DreamRec implements this idea with guided diffusion. A transformer encodes the historical interaction sequence into a guidance representation. During learning, adding noise to target items explores the distribution of the item space. The guided denoising process then generates an idealized item intended to recover the positive item associated with that history.

This changes the learning objective from classifying sampled candidates to generating an item representation conditioned on previous interactions, removing the need for negative sampling. The imagined ideal item is the paper's modeling perspective on preference, rather than a directly observed statement of a user's wishes. The authors evaluate DreamRec through extensive experiments and comparisons with existing methods, examining the effectiveness of this generative recommendation approach.
neurips-2023-generate-what-you-prefer-re.tldr: DreamRec uses history-guided diffusion to generate an idealized next-item representation without negative sampling.

paragraphs: Stein discrepancies are statistical tools used to assess approximations, support inference, and construct sampling methods. Their standard forms require derivatives of the statistical model. In complicated models, computing those derivatives reliably can demand specialized numerical algorithms, making an otherwise useful discrepancy difficult to apply in practice.

This paper introduces a collection of alternative Stein discrepancies that do not require model derivatives. Its focus is posterior approximation: working with an approximation to the distribution of unknown quantities after observing data. The change targets the derivative requirement itself, allowing the authors to investigate discrepancy-based posterior methods without relying on that particular computational ingredient.

The authors establish sufficient conditions under which the new discrepancies detect and control convergence, and present applications to sampling and variational inference. These guarantees are conditional on the stated sufficient conditions, rather than automatic consequences of avoiding gradients. The significance is that removing model derivatives need not mean abandoning mathematical convergence guarantees: the paper develops both derivative-free constructions and a theoretical account of when they remain informative.
neurips-2023-gradient-free-kernel-stein-.tldr: New gradient-free Stein discrepancies support posterior approximation and retain convergence guarantees under sufficient conditions.

paragraphs: Hyper-Skin is a dataset for learning to reconstruct detailed facial skin spectra from RGB images. Its measurements span visible wavelengths from 400 to 700 nanometers and near-infrared wavelengths from 700 to 1000 nanometers. The intended research direction is to make richer skin analysis accessible from the images available on consumer devices.

The dataset contains 330 hyperspectral cubes collected from 51 people with a pushbroom hyperspectral camera, covering different viewing angles and facial poses. Each cube contains 1024 by 1024 spatial positions and 448 spectral channels. The authors pair these measurements with synthetic RGB images generated using real camera responses, connecting the detailed spectral observations to ordinary three-channel image inputs.

To demonstrate the dataset's usefulness, the authors apply existing reconstruction models to 31 resampled bands spanning visible and near-infrared wavelengths. The resource supports research into spectral properties associated with quantities such as melanin and hemoglobin concentrations. Its contribution is paired data and a reconstruction demonstration that enable such investigations, with data-request instructions and benchmarking code made publicly available.
neurips-2023-hyper-skin-a-hyperspectral-.tldr: Hyper-Skin pairs detailed facial hyperspectral measurements with synthetic RGB images to support skin-spectrum reconstruction research.

paragraphs: Gradient clipping limits the size of noisy optimization updates. This paper studies its convergence when noise has heavy tails, assuming a bounded pth moment for some p greater than one and at most two. The goal is a guarantee that holds with high probability, rather than only describing average behavior over repeated runs.

Previous analyses control successive iterations with concentration inequalities and a union bound, introducing a factor equal to the number of iterations into the failure probability. The authors instead bound the moment generating function of a carefully selected supermartingale sequence. This improves the iteration-count dependence for clipped mirror-descent methods on convex objectives and clipped stochastic gradient descent on nonconvex objectives.

The resulting high-probability guarantees achieve optimal convergence rates and match the best known bounds in expectation. The analysis also accommodates changing step sizes and clipping thresholds without knowing the training horizon in advance. For clipped stochastic mirror descent, parameter choices additionally avoid requiring several problem constants, including the initial distance to the optimum, making the theoretical prescription less dependent on unavailable quantities.
neurips-2023-improved-convergence-in-hig.tldr: A new analysis strengthens high-probability convergence guarantees for clipped optimization under heavy-tailed noise and supports unknown training horizons.

paragraphs: Programming usually involves running code, inspecting what happened, and revising the next step. Many coding benchmarks instead evaluate a single conversion from instructions into code. InterCode makes the execution-and-revision loop part of the benchmark, allowing models to respond to errors, clarify behavior, and tackle tasks through multiple interactions.

The framework represents interactive coding as a reinforcement-learning environment: code is an action, and execution feedback is an observation. Self-contained Docker environments support safe, reproducible execution. InterCode is designed to work across languages and platforms, accommodate existing sequence-to-sequence coding methods, and support methods developed specifically for interactive generation.

The authors create Bash, SQL, and Python environments from existing static datasets and evaluate language models with prompting strategies including ReAct and Plan & Solve. Their results show benefits from interactive generation while establishing a challenging testbed. The framework is also extensible to tasks such as Capture the Flag, where several steps and programming languages may be needed. Its contribution is a common way to study coding as an ongoing process.
neurips-2023-intercode-standardizing-and.tldr: InterCode benchmarks coding as an interactive process in which models execute code and use feedback to guide subsequent actions.

paragraphs: Learning with limited labeled data often means adding unlabeled examples, transferring knowledge from another dataset, or creating augmented examples. This paper examines another source of information already present in the data: the meaning of labels expressed in natural language. Labels can carry relationships that are lost when they function only as category identifiers.

The proposed Language Semantic Graph represents those descriptions in graph form. An auxiliary graph neural network learns higher-level semantic relationships from the graph and uses them to guide the primary model's training. The approach therefore gives label meaning an explicit role in learning, aiming to make fuller use of the supervision that is already available.

The authors apply this method to transfer learning and semi-supervised learning across images, video, and audio. They report significant improvements over other approaches to data-efficient learning, and their analysis also finds faster training. These findings support the usefulness of semantic label relationships across the tested modalities and learning settings, with an auxiliary graph providing a shared mechanism for conveying that information.
neurips-2023-language-semantic-graph-gui.tldr: A graph built from natural-language labels guides model training, improving data efficiency and training speed in the evaluated settings.

paragraphs: The efficient coding hypothesis proposes that sensory systems adapt to capture as much environmental information as biological constraints permit. Testing this idea computationally is difficult because information-based objectives can be hard to measure or optimize. This paper studies manifold capacity, a measure of how many object categories a representation can make separable by linear decision rules.

Calculating that capacity normally requires an expensive iterative procedure. The authors describe simplifying assumptions that allow it to be optimized directly, producing Maximum Manifold Capacity Representations, or MMCR. The resulting method is closely connected to self-supervised learning, turning a theoretically motivated efficiency measure into a usable representation-learning objective.

MMCR is competitive with leading methods on standard self-supervised benchmarks. Empirical analysis also identifies differences from other learned representations and suggests a mechanism linking manifold compression to category separation. In neural prediction benchmarks, MMCR is highly competitive as a model of the ventral visual stream. These results connect representation quality with biological modeling, while the proposed compression mechanism remains an interpretation suggested by the empirical findings.
neurips-2023-learning-efficient-coding-o.tldr: MMCR makes manifold capacity directly optimizable under simplifying assumptions, producing competitive visual representations and models of ventral-stream responses.

paragraphs: Language models normally give each token a fixed learned representation. This paper asks whether a model can instead infer meaning entirely from patterns of repetition and co-occurrence within its context. A lexinvariant model does not depend on the identities assigned to lexical symbols, forcing contextual structure to carry the information.

The implementation assigns random Gaussian vectors to tokens, keeping a token's vector consistent within a sequence but changing it across sequences. The authors prove that a lexinvariant model can be constructed to converge to the true language model at a uniform rate polynomial in context length, with a constant factor sublinear in vocabulary size. Empirically, comparable perplexity requires sufficiently long context.

The models also infer substitution-cipher mappings with high accuracy, behavior described as implicit Bayesian deciphering in context. On synthetic in-context reasoning tasks, they achieve four times better accuracy on average. These findings show how much token meaning can be recovered from structure in the tested settings and motivate exploring lexinvariance as a regularizer for standard language models.
neurips-2023-lexinvariant-language-model.tldr: Lexinvariant language models replace fixed token embeddings with sequence-specific random vectors and can achieve comparable perplexity with sufficiently long context.

paragraphs: Estimating movement in images and explaining human motion perception are closely related problems, but success at one does not automatically establish success at the other. This paper develops an image-based model intended to connect biological accounts of visual motion with the ability of computer-vision systems to process complex natural scenes.

Its two-stage architecture combines trainable motion-energy sensing with a recurrent self-attention network. The first stage senses motion, while the second adaptively integrates or separates motion information. The architecture aims to capture computations associated with the V1–MT visual pathway while remaining capable of producing informative motion flow across a wide range of stimuli.

Simulated neurophysiology finds similarities between model units and mammalian recordings in motion pooling and speed tuning. The model also reproduces human responses to several psychophysical stimuli. On Sintel, its outputs predict human responses better than ground-truth motion does, whereas leading computer-vision models show the opposite pattern. These findings support its value as a perceptual model, although the authors explicitly acknowledge that physiological correspondence may be inexact.
neurips-2023-modeling-human-visual-motio.tldr: A motion-sensing and recurrent-attention model reproduces several human and neural motion responses while processing complex natural scenes.

paragraphs: Spherical harmonics describe functions on a sphere through components of different degrees. This paper asks how many function evaluations are needed to recover the expansion through a chosen degree. The objective is robust reconstruction with a sample count close to the number of independent components in the desired expansion.

For any square-integrable function on the unit sphere, the authors show that the required evaluations match the dimension of the harmonic space through degree q, apart from a logarithmic factor. This ties the sampling requirement to the size of the representation being recovered. The result applies in any ambient dimension d.

The proposed algorithm uses kernel regression and evaluates the function at uniformly sampled points on the sphere. Its construction draws on connections between spherical harmonics and Gegenbauer polynomials. Unlike the prior fast-transform results discussed in the abstract, it combines efficient reconstruction with nearly optimal sampling across dimensions. Numerical examples illustrate its empirical behavior, complementing the theoretical result about how economically a truncated harmonic expansion can be recovered.
neurips-2023-near-optimal-reconstruction.tldr: A kernel-regression algorithm reconstructs spherical harmonic expansions from uniformly sampled evaluations with a sample count optimal up to a logarithmic factor.

paragraphs: Distributional robustness trains against unfavorable changes in a distribution. Much previous work applies this idea to the data distribution. This paper instead considers distributions over models, asking how to train a central model distribution so that nearby distributions cannot increase the loss too much.

The neighborhood is a Wasserstein ball, defined using optimal transport. Within that neighborhood, the framework examines the model distribution that maximizes loss, and the authors develop theory for learning the robust center. Different choices of center connect the formulation to a single model, an ensemble with uniform weights, or a Bayesian neural network.

This provides a shared account of sharpness-aware training across those settings. In particular, Sharpness-Aware Minimization appears as a special case when the center puts all its probability on one model; the broader framework extends that idea probabilistically. Experiments across the single-model, ensemble, and Bayesian settings report substantial improvements over the evaluated baselines. The contribution is both a unifying formulation and empirical evidence for training with robustness in model space.
neurips-2023-optimal-transport-model-dis.tldr: An optimal-transport framework extends sharpness-aware training to distributions over single models, ensembles, and Bayesian neural networks.

paragraphs: Curriculum learning presents simpler examples before harder ones. Although experiments have often found benefits, proving an advantage under comparable training conditions is difficult. This paper studies parity learning with data drawn from a mixture of sparse and dense inputs, comparing training schedules on a common underlying sample distribution.

The authors identify a regime in which a two-layer ReLU network can learn sufficiently high-degree parity targets by training on sparse examples first. Their curriculum algorithms use noisy gradient descent or stochastic gradient descent with bounded learning rates. The comparison shows that fully connected networks trained by noisy gradient descent on unordered samples require additional steps, even if they have greater width or depth.

The result establishes a training-step separation within the specified regime, making example order a provable source of advantage under those conditions. It extends beyond earlier one-step arguments involving large learning rates. Experiments also support a similar qualitative separation outside the exact theoretical regime, providing broader empirical evidence without extending the theorem's formal scope to every curriculum or dataset.
neurips-2023-provable-advantage-of-curri.tldr: For a specified mixed-input parity-learning regime, sparse-first curriculum training provably needs fewer steps than noisy gradient descent on unordered samples.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning learns behavior from a fixed dataset. The variety of demonstrated actions can differ sharply between situations: drivers may behave similarly at a red light but very differently when merging. This paper examines why a uniform requirement to resemble the recorded behavior can be poorly suited to such uneven variability.

The authors provide theoretical and empirical evidence that typical distribution-constrained methods can fail in this setting. Their proposed principle lets a policy choose how closely to follow demonstrated behavior separately for each state, while remaining within its support. That preserves a restriction to supported actions without demanding the same degree of distributional similarity everywhere.

CQL (ReDS) approximates this support constraint by reweighting the data distribution in conservative Q-learning. The reweighted distribution mixes the current policy with another policy trained to identify poor actions that are nevertheless likely in the recorded behavior. The method improves performance across evaluated games, navigation tasks, and pixel-based manipulation problems, supporting state-dependent flexibility when demonstrations vary unevenly in quality and diversity.
neurips-2023-reds-offline-rl-with-hetero.tldr: CQL (ReDS) uses an approximate support constraint to adapt how closely an offline policy follows demonstrations in each state.

paragraphs: People with multiple conditions may need several medications, making both personalization and interactions between drugs relevant to recommendation. The paper identifies two shortcomings in existing systems: recommendations restricted to broad medication classes and interaction models that treat all drug interactions as equally severe. REFINE is designed to provide more fine-grained recommendations.

To represent a patient's condition, REFINE models trends in dosage adjustments and laboratory-test responses. It adapts a vision transformer to build patient representations from this information. Drug interactions are represented as weighted graphs, allowing the model to distinguish severity levels when learning combinations of medications.

The training objective also balances competing concerns. Avoiding interactions too aggressively could omit drugs needed for a patient's conditions, so the authors introduce a loss intended to prevent overly conservative recommendations. Experiments on two real-world datasets show better performance than the compared state-of-the-art techniques. These findings support the recommendation method in the evaluated datasets; improved treatment outcomes and fewer adverse interactions are the system's design aims.
neurips-2023-refine-a-fine-grained-medic.tldr: REFINE combines dosage and laboratory trends with severity-weighted drug-interaction graphs to improve fine-grained medication recommendations.

paragraphs: Diffusion planners generate trajectories and guide them toward desired outcomes, which has shown promise for long tasks with sparse rewards. However, a generated trajectory may include transitions that cannot actually be executed. This paper addresses that reliability problem by detecting error-prone plans and supplying guidance intended to refine them.

The authors introduce a plan-quality metric called the restoration gap. A learned gap predictor estimates this quantity and produces guidance for the diffusion planner. Because an imperfect predictor can itself provide adversarial refining guidance, the method also includes an attribution-map regularizer intended to prevent that behavior and improve refinement of infeasible plans.

Experiments on three offline-control benchmarks requiring long-horizon planning demonstrate the approach's effectiveness. The predictor's attribution maps also highlight transitions associated with errors, giving an interpretable view of which parts of a plan need attention. The contribution combines quality estimation, corrective guidance, and explanations of problematic transitions. It addresses the stated lack of feasibility guarantees through empirical refinement, without establishing that every resulting plan is feasible.
neurips-2023-refining-diffusion-planner-.tldr: A restoration-gap predictor guides diffusion planners away from infeasible trajectories, with attribution-based regularization and explanations of error-prone transitions.

paragraphs: Visual query localization asks where and when a visually specified object appears in a long first-person video. This capability matters for episodic-memory systems that must retrieve past visual experiences. Existing approaches combine several independently trained detection and tracking stages, creating complex pipelines with slow inference.

VQLoC replaces that arrangement with a single-stage framework trained end to end. It first builds a joint understanding of the query and video by considering two kinds of correspondence: matches between the query and individual frames, and relationships between nearby frames. It then uses that combined information to localize the object across space and time in one shot.

The experiments report a 20% accuracy improvement over prior visual-query localization methods alongside a tenfold inference-speed improvement. The abstract also reports VQLoC as the leading entry on the Ego4D VQ2D challenge leaderboard. These results support jointly modeling object appearance and temporal relationships within a unified system, with the evaluated method improving both localization performance and the speed of producing an answer.
neurips-2023-single-stage-visual-query-l.tldr: VQLoC jointly models query-to-frame and frame-to-frame relationships, reporting better localization accuracy and tenfold faster inference than prior methods.

paragraphs: Complex interactive tasks require an agent to choose actions while keeping track of broader goals. SwiftSage approaches this by combining two kinds of decision-making, inspired by the distinction between fast and deliberate human thought. Its central design joins behavior learned from demonstrations with planning supplied by a large language model.

The Swift component is a small encoder-decoder language model fine-tuned on an oracle agent's action trajectories. It supplies the fast, intuitive side of the framework. The Sage component uses a model such as GPT-4 to plan subgoals and ground them in the task. A heuristic integration method coordinates the two components into one action-planning system.

Across 30 ScienceWorld tasks, SwiftSage significantly outperforms methods including SayCan, ReAct, and Reflexion. The authors present the combined process as more efficient and robust, with these results demonstrating its effectiveness on complex interactive tasks in that benchmark. The contribution is the coordinated architecture: a compact model trained on successful action sequences works together with a larger model responsible for deliberate planning.
neurips-2023-swiftsage-a-generative-agen.tldr: SwiftSage combines a small imitation-trained action model with deliberate LLM planning and significantly outperforms compared agents on 30 ScienceWorld tasks.

paragraphs: A diffusion model's intermediate state changes throughout generation, but the structure of that space is not fully understood. This paper investigates it geometrically, focusing on the latent state at a particular diffusion timestep. The authors use the model's encoding feature maps to define a pullback metric and derive a local set of latent directions.

Those directions provide a way to edit an image: move the intermediate state along a discovered basis vector at a selected timestep. The demonstrated procedure makes its edit once and requires no additional training. This connects the geometric analysis to a concrete intervention in the generation process.

The authors also examine how the geometry changes over time and under different text conditions. Their findings confirm coarse-to-fine generation and reveal differences between latent states across timesteps, effects of dataset complexity, and a changing influence of text prompts. The resulting account treats diffusion's latent structure as time-dependent, helping explain why the timestep and conditioning matter when interpreting or manipulating an intermediate representation.
neurips-2023-understanding-the-latent-sp.tldr: Geometric analysis reveals local diffusion-state directions that enable single-timestep image edits without additional training.

paragraphs: Deep-learning-based variational Monte Carlo can produce highly accurate quantum-chemistry calculations, but optimizing a new model for every molecule is expensive. This paper proposes reusing a neural wavefunction model pretrained through self-supervised optimization on a large, chemically diverse collection of molecules. The aim is to transfer that work to new molecular problems.

The model combines an improved geometry embedding with an existing SE(3)-equivariant architecture for molecular orbitals. Training also continuously samples geometries. Together, these choices improve zero-shot accuracy by two orders of magnitude relative to the state of the art reported by the authors, making pretrained predictions substantially more useful before molecule-specific optimization.

On new molecules, the model produces wavefunctions and absolute energies without further optimization that outperform established methods such as CCSD(T)-2Z. Accurate relative energies still require a few fine-tuning steps. That distinction separates immediate reuse from the additional adaptation needed for energy differences. The authors evaluate accuracy, scalability, and limitations across varied test systems, supporting pretraining as a way to reduce repeated optimization costs.
neurips-2023-variational-monte-carlo-on-.tldr: Pretrained neural wavefunctions deliver strong zero-shot molecular predictions, while a few fine-tuning steps provide accurate relative energies.
